newsitem.title: USA: Marzook pleads no contest to "terror" charges.
newsitem.headline: Marzook pleads no contest to "terror" charges.

text.p: The political leader of the Islamic Resistance Movement Hamas, Mousa Abu Marzook, pleaded no contest to charges of involvement in "terrorist activity" before he was deported by the United States on Monday, immigration officials said.

In agreeing to be deported, Abu Marzook entered into what in legal terms is called "a plea of nolo contendere" which means that he did not contest the exclusion charges that had been brought against him, the Immigration and Naturalisation Service said.
"These charges state that Abu Marzook is an alien who has engaged in a terrorist activity or ... who is likely after entry to engage in terrorist activity," the INS said in a statement.
A plea of "nolo contendere" is merely a disposition of a case without a finding or admission, lawyers said.
Defence lawyer Michael Kennedy said that in the agreement Abu Marzook signed, "he has not admitted being a terrorist and continues to maintain that he is not, and has never been a terrorist."
Kennedy said that in the agreement Abu Marzook vehemently denied the charges and "denies he has ever participated in terrorist activities or intends to ever participate in terrorist activities."

In a statement before leaving New York, Marzook said: "While the INS ... sought to exclude me on the pretext that I am a terrorist, it nevertheless negotiated a written agreement with me and conceded to allowing me to emphatically deny the charges in the agreement."
Abu Marzook was deported to Jordan on Monday after almost two years in a federal jail in lower Manhattan.

Abu Marzook, 46, was arrested on July 25, 1995 at John F. Kennedy International Airport as he flew back to the United States -- where he had lived for many years -- after immigration officials found his name on its "watch list" of people with "known or suspected ties to terrorist activities."

Israel had requested his arrest and his extradition, alleging that he was involved in a number of fatal bombings, shootings and stabbings between 1990 and 1994 and had raised money for and controlled the leadership of the military wing of Hamas.
In January, Abu Marzook asked to be turned over to the Jewish State for trial but Israel withdrew its extradition request on April 6.
Abu Marzook maintained throughout his detention that he was only involved in political activities while in Amman.
